record_notes.DCP-LETT-1688: May 27, supplied 1855. Explicitly answers an unlocated Hooker note about newspaper reporting, sea transport and continental extension. Distinguishes planned flotation of whole herbaceous plants from observed closure of immersed pods and composite heads. Seeks only possibility of some transport over long ages, not proof of all distribution. Requests Watson Azores references, Saxifrage and Hedysarum; conditions about plant tenderness remain questions. Photograph self-criticism and Viola floral observation are Darwin voice. Carpenter appreciation is Hooker reported news; later December journal edition publication is future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1692: June 2, supplied 1855. Cancels the Azorean paper search requested May 27 after a bad week with his stomach and loss of enthusiasm. Same-author reversal of his own request, not an incoming reply. Later renewed trials are separate events. Do not diagnose beyond historical self-report.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1693: June 5, supplied 1855. Thanks for Saxifrage and a missing Hooker note, reports six of seven kinds germinated after fifty-six days and distinct cabbage/broccoli/cauliflower outcomes, and jokingly invokes Vestiges in discussing Tussilago seedlings. Field comparison with Thorley is underway, not completed. Direct raw DOM verifies MathML in Hedysarum proposal is half an hour daily, not twelve hours. Transmission route depends on tenderness. Explicitly has Gray kind letter and habitat list forwarded through Hooker; Gray May 22 source 1685 is known by this day. Requests clarification of Hooker continental preference. Cannot answer 1694, which was composed June 6–9 after this source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1694: Hooker June 6–9, 1855 fragment, original XML bounded range. Responds to June 5 Hedysarum transport/tenderness and continental preference, offers Mimosa, objects to sea transport by regional uniformity and New Zealand absences, and discusses distribution of lower orders, creation and transmutation. Several theories remain unsatisfactory to him; he is not simply committed to continental extension. Missing top and bottom page portions and incomplete final clause are retained, not filled from Darwin annotations. Asks to see Gray letter, having evidently not read it merely by forwarding it. Later Darwin notes are undated and partly address content absent from surviving body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1696: June 10, supplied 1855. Direct response to 1694 includes Mimosa acceptance, distinction between demonstrated Britain-continent union and speculative oceanic connections, New Zealand absences, distribution of low plants, and species ancestry versus first origin of life. Frog-spawn salt resistance remains an assumption to test. Sends Gray material because earlier forwarding did not establish Hooker read it. Salt resistance is only one small step toward distribution explanation, not proof of migration. P1–9 and P11–13 are supported response scope; Berkeley outcome enquiry P10 and Rhododendrum update P14 are separate topics. No precise receipt date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1700: June 15 with supplied month/year. Hedysarum physically received, fulfilling the earlier offer, but no dispatch note survives. Grass naming, Hooker reaction to retrograde-step criticism and Godron discussion require missing intervening material, so no whole-letter pair with 1694. Interested in Florula Juvenalis by June 15; bibliography records completion June 16, not a contradiction requiring silent date change. Plans future Azores work and reports puzzling orchid observations, without assuming successful self-fertilisation from swelling alone.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1702: June 23 with supplied month/year. Found Watson paper at Linnean Society yesterday, June 22, and borrowed four volumes in Sir William name under Hooker prior arrangement. Finding/borrowing does not prove whole-paper reading that day; July reading record is separate. Turtle-soup and wine advice is historical jocular prose, not current health guidance. Previous Hooker loan arrangement is background rather than an incoming message made from this outgoing note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1711: July 5, supplied 1855. Requests identification of a grass, doubtful even of Festuca and confident it is not F. pratensis, after collecting thirty-five kinds. Postscript reports several species germinating after eighty-five days in salt water. Hooker 1714 supplies the contrary identification. Preserve thirty-five in Darwin versus thirty in Hooker reply; no silent numerical harmonisation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1714: Supplied July 8, 1855, Sunday after July 5 request. Hooker identifies grass as Festuca pratensis and comments on poor fit to descriptions. Continues with Australian Leguminosae, about nine hundred species, four hundred fifty southwest and three hundred southeast with fewer than ten shared; this is not a claim all nine hundred are accounted for in those two counts. Describes Himalayan thistles bridging English forms and uncertainty over species distinctions. Powell disappointment is Hooker opinion. Reverse reply to 1711; later Darwin annotations are not same-day knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1717: July 14 with supplied month/year. P2–3 directly thank Hooker for Festuca identification and answer Australian flora, thistle intermediates and poor descriptions. P1 enclosure for Lindley is identified only probably by editors; do not promote that to certainty. P4 Hunt/Daubeny enquiry concerns planned glass experiments, not completed results. P5 explicitly forwards Watson July 11 list, with red-marked Henslow items and request for additional seed sources. P6 corrects list versus actual seed supply, pointing to missing Hooker note; P7 hybridism/Dianthus and P9 expected baby are additional enquiries. Direct reply scope P2–3 only; Watson evidence is separate cross-correspondent knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1719: July 18 with supplied month/year. Responds to missing birth announcement and Daubeny communication; Flora Indica arrived this morning, not proof that its introduction has been read. A Madeira essay was read, with author attribution partly conjectured by Darwin. Eyre desert comparison in P2 plausibly continues July 8 Australian discussion, but intervening Hooker note is missing, so no uniquely demonstrated new pair. P8 explicitly answers a question about extent of common descent absent from 1714. Preserve that missing prompt rather than turn generic species discussion into its text. Yesterday forty-first grass is a dated observation; old London Clay seed report is rejected by Darwin, not validated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1722: July 19, supplied 1855. Explicitly received Gray enclosure through Hooker, identified by marked-sheet promise as June 30 source 1707. Letter receipt does not mean promised annotated sheets arrived. Defers seed list work, comments on Daubeny and gives safer future parcel route. No exact physical receipt day or surviving Hooker cover established. Instructions about delivery remain historical content.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1731: July 28 with supplied month/year. Invites Hooker to August 7 dinner with Henslow; no acceptance shown. Just received a separate magnificent illustrated work and is in the middle of Flora Indica, not finished. Missing Bunbury note praised that Flora; do not substitute April Bunbury mountain letter 1664. Mrs Hooker congratulations follow birth news.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1737: August 10, supplied 1855. Missing Hooker note carried Lindley invitation. Darwin accepted then cancelled after illness and home news; meeting did not occur on this evidence. Morning with Watson actually took place and supplied oral seed-longevity cautions. Requests Godron paper from Nancy memoirs, not yet acquired. Hooker European tour is imminent, not complete; exact travel date not set by this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1738: August 11, supplied 1855. Reports leaving Henslow handbook at Athenaeum and asks whether Gray marked sheets were included or would come later. This reflects June 30 Gray promise, not receipt of those sheets. Future routing through Sir William is conditional. Pigeon character discovery is author statement without specified anatomical character; later Variation identification must not be inserted. 1722 is another Darwin outgoing letter, never its incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1741: August 14 with supplied month/year. A new Gray letter/enclosed Hooker note arrived this morning, but that letter is missing; it corrects prior expected proof sheets to manuscript list. Do not treat June 30 source as this morning arrival. Requests Manual loan and names three Erfurt growers matching Cattell August 13, seeking advice on separation and selection rather than trade. Flora Indica almost finished, not completed. Later Natural selection barnacle narrative is quoted apparatus, not part of this letter. Lindley missed visit remains a regret.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1742: October 18 with supplied month/year, Thursday evening. Sends two Norwegian seeds from Lofoten and Alten, says they floated ten days, asks naming and planting. This advances his October 10 plan but both letters are Darwin outgoing, not a Q/A pair. Ten-day claim is preserved without inventing an exact experimental start date from approximate sequence. P3 thanks a missing interesting Hooker letter. Hooker names Mucuna and Entada scandens question-mark written at head are quoted by editor, separate from Darwin text. Club attendance is prospective.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1685: Additional full reading of Gray May 22, 1855. Answers an unlocated-in-this-packet Darwin request and returns a completed habitat list, while offering fuller comparison and requesting methodological hints. North American flora plans remain prospective; last volumes were not in fact completed as expected. Alpine plant identities and Labrador occurrence include confidence levels and pending re-examination. Mountain distances in P7 were later corrected, not silently replaced in May text. Darwin marginal annotation below signature is cut off. No full enclosure transcription here. June 5 Hooker letter demonstrates Darwin reading this Gray letter and list; forwarding alone does not demonstrate Hooker read it.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1707: Additional full reading of Gray June 30, 1855, explicitly answering June 8. Promises annotated Manual sheets with close species, discusses taxonomy and burden of evidence, plans newspaper reprinting and Morris fish-egg enquiry. Distinguish proposed sheets from later manuscript delivery and planned enquiry from already dispatched Morris June 17 letter described by editors. P12–14 correct earlier road-like distances to about seventy-five and sixty direct miles; retain correction chronology. Notes are undated. Bibliography includes unrelated George Robert Gray bird genera entry; do not confuse author identity with Asa Gray or treat that entry as letter voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1739: Additional full reading of Cattell August 13, 1855. In answer to missing Darwin enquiry, says he imports German seed directly and names Platz, Haage and Appelius at Erfurt, plus Behn at Hamburg, with quality and demand claims. These are Cattell commercial observations, not Darwin experiments. Distinctive first-three-grower sequence is reused in Darwin August 14 Hooker enquiry. That proves reading by August 14, not exact physical receipt; morning receipt in 1741 is of Gray enclosure.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1671: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with accepted note/ledger and matching source pins. April 24 with supplied 1855 year thanks Sir William through Joseph for a gift, explicitly contrasted with the originally requested loan; not merely a loan acknowledgement. Identification as Lawsonian synopsis is editorially probable. A missing Hooker question asks whether seeds float: all sink after hours except beet, with shaking to encourage sinking. Hooker expectation of death after a week is reported but the underlying note is missing. Darwin reports cress/lettuce germination after twenty-one days and postpones a further experiment because of cold ground. The seeds-already-reached-islands argument is from another unidentified letter, not Hooker by default. A separate April 13 experimental note quoted by editors cannot be silently merged with April 24 composition.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1680: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with accepted note/ledger and matching source pins. May 11 with supplied 1855 year, Darwin to Hooker. Explicitly received note just now brings assistant-director appointment news, not the later directorship itself. Salary and expected promotion are qualified; he promises discretion. A missing note also asks about Job, publication venue, Kerguelen insects and club matters. Westminster article location and proposed loan are separate from modern attribution to Froude. Seed report to Lindley is planned and later permanent publication conditional; May 26 and 1856 publications are later events. The two-sex moth detail is absent from 1644, so P4 is not uniquely a delayed reply to that older source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1681: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with accepted note/ledger and matching source pins. May 15, supplied month/year from fish experiment evidence, Darwin to Hooker, not an incoming Hooker response. Two Hooker notes and Scoresby dry but useful answer are unlocated. The MathML in P2 is 1/2 hour, not twelve hours talking to Sabine. P3 imagined fish/heron transport fails when the fish eject the seeds; do not train imagined success as observed result. P4 future fresh-seed and pod/branch flotation trials are prospective; later May 17 note cannot be projected into May 15. P5–6 and P9 request Mimosa/Guillandina and Lofoten seed trials, distinguish Robert Brown report and Keeling recollection, and end with 1000-to-1 doubt. P7 criticises De La Rue exclusion while praising his council conduct. Same-author 1680 is not its incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1715: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with accepted note/ledger and matching source pins. Additional full reading: Watson July 11, supplied 1855, returns Darwin Azores list with distribution markings and a second list of species least likely introduced by people. Its existence and purpose are explicit, but its complete seventy-eight entries are not transcribed here; do not invent the enclosure from the letter or Darwin twenty-two selections. P2 guesses many species arrived by human agency; P3 mentions possible Madeira transit. Footnote 2 quotes Watson marking legend, a separate voice from Darwin. Darwin salting annotation is undated. Later witness 1718 explicitly dates receipt of the list to July 13 and demonstrates using its criterion.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1763: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with accepted note/ledger and matching source pins. Additional full reading, October 10 supplied 1855. Mrs Hooker supplies return/move news, not necessarily a Joseph Hooker incoming letter. Seeds from Kew arrived about ten to fourteen days earlier and are distinct from the two Norwegian seeds. Darwin explicitly has the latter and plans ten-day flotation followed by naming and planting at Kew; those stages are not complete on this evidence. Capsicum/celery germinated after 137 days. Glasgow letter remains missing, Gourlie kindness is a remembered event, and Candolle is being read rather than necessarily finished. This proves Crowe seed-shipment information was known by October 10, earlier than the November direct reply.

reading_method: Seventeen targets plus extra Gray 1685/1707 and Cattell 1739 independently read in full. Target 1763, three assigned contexts and extra Watson 1715 reuse explicit primary full-reading records with matching pins. Read original XML attributes, all bodies, exclusions, missing-page markers, annotations, footnotes and bibliography. Raw DOM confirms half-hour MathML in 1693. No inline figure.
